correctness.rationale: At any state with x clique and y independent unmatched vertices of K_x∨bar(K_y), eligible clique edges number x(x−1)/2 and cross edges xy; the next uniformly sampled edge is therefore internal with probability (x−1)/(x−1+2y) and crossing with probability 2y/(x−1+2y). Conditioning gives the stated finite rational distribution recursion and exact endpoints. Independent small-state rational recursion reproduced representative terminal laws and matching-size parity. For a_n/n→α>0,b_n/n→β>0, exponential edge clocks of rate 1/n yield fluid drift dx/dt=−x²−xy,dy/dt=−xy. The first integral x/y−log(y/β)=α/β leads to terminal survivor y*=βe^(−α/β). Uniform drift/martingale estimates justify endpoint convergence; stopping when x<=εn controls late survivors. The finite-parameter invariant H_n=x/y−log(y/β_n)−r_n has jumps O(1/n) and conditional drift O(1/n²) per accepted match; its centered martingale bracket converges to [4−e^(−r)(r+2)²]/y*. A stopping argument keeps the late part O(ε²), allowing martingale CLT and delta method Y centered at z_n=b_n exp(−a_n/b_n) with variance v=βe^(−r)[4−e^(−r)(r+2)²]. This v>0 for r>0. Matching size differs from (a+b−Y)/2 by at most 1/2, preserving the CLT. The maximum matching size is min(a,floor((a+b)/2)); differentiating the two branches of the asymptotic efficiency ratio gives a unique minimum at r=1 of 1−1/(2e). The finite exact solver check.py was read; full-edge-order enumeration and simulations corroborate only finite cases, not the stopped martingale limit.

value.rationale: Uniform random-EDGE maximal matching is a canonical greedy algorithm, and complete split graphs are a simple structured dense obstruction to optimality. The exact finite law, Gaussian survivor fluctuations, and sharp worst balance ratio quantify both algorithmic performance and variability rather than a tiny graph example. In particular a split graph with a perfect matching can lose a nonzero 1/(2e) fraction asymptotically under uniform greedy edge ordering; the variance is a reproducible natural statistic for randomized-algorithm benchmarks.
